sealed_statement.scope: For one authoritative hard state P and one compatible forced assignment set F, compare only authorized histories that are jointly reachable and request exactly F.
sealed_statement.confluence: All nonterminal such histories have the same B2B1 canonical closure up to canonical relabeling and semantically equivalent independent reconstruction receipts. Terminal UNSAT outcomes are also order-independent.
sealed_statement.state_coordinates: The final remaining graph, final forced/fixed assignments, source classes, exact palettes, residual components, C0 messages, C2 incidences, B2A signatures and C3 selectors depend on F and not on the forcing order.
sealed_statement.reconstruction: Earlier deleted repair components have no nonfixed outside neighbors when deleted; later jointly reachable forces cannot change their exact local obligations. Reconstruction therefore commutes as a factorized collection of independent component receipts.
sealed_statement.history_collapse: Forcing history/order is not an additional state coordinate. State enumeration may quotient histories by their compatible forced assignment set followed by canonical closure.

proof_core.fixed_effects: Final seed-color effects are set unions and are order-independent.
proof_core.singleton_persistence: Under monotone seed growth, a source singleton remains the same singleton or becomes Z0; a nonterminal compatible continuation excludes Z0.
proof_core.X0_uniqueness: The final source-singleton promotion set is therefore uniquely determined by F.
proof_core.partition_uniqueness: Final source partition and exact palettes are deterministic functions of final S and X0.
proof_core.repair_commutation: Monotone X0 growth can only disconnect further; already deleted components have no nonfixed outside dependencies and cannot be affected by future jointly reachable forcing.
proof_core.downstream_determinism: C0/C2/B2A/C3 are deterministic recompilations of the same final canonical state.

explicit_nonclaims: No polynomial bound on compatible forced assignment sets.
No polynomial canonical quotient on those sets.
No theorem erasing identities of newly forced seed vertices.
